thesis: Lam Research is the #2 global wafer fabrication equipment maker (after Applied Materials) and the dominant supplier of etch and deposition tools — the two most critical process steps for 3D NAND, advanced DRAM/HBM, and gate-all-around (GAA) logic. FY2026 revenue grew 26% to $23.2B with Q4 reaching $6.72B (+30% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.82 (+37% YoY). The AI buildout structurally favors Lam: every additional 3D NAND layer, every HBM stack, and the GAA transistor transition require more etch and deposition steps. The board approved a 27% dividend increase. At ~48x trailing P/E, the stock is moderately valued for a WFE leader in a cyclical upcycle. Key risks are WFE cyclicality, China export controls (~30% of revenue historically), and customer concentration.

drivers: 3D NAND layer count increases (300+ layers) require proportionally more etch/dep steps, expanding Lam's SAM
HBM and advanced DRAM packaging drive incremental WFE spending at TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix
GAA transistor transition at leading-edge foundries increases etch complexity and Lam's content per wafer
FY2027 guidance reflects continued WFE upcycle with potential re-acceleration from AI capex

base_case.assumptions: FY2027 revenue grows 10–15% as WFE spending normalizes from peak growth rates. Gross margins stabilize near 48–50%. EPS reaches ~$7.00–7.50. Market applies 65–75x trailing P/E, reflecting cyclical premium at mid-cycle.

risks: WFE cyclical downturn as memory and logic fabs complete current investment wave
Tightening China export controls further restrict ~30% of Lam's addressable market
TSMC or Samsung capex cuts in response to demand normalization
Broad semiconductor de-rating driven by AI investment ROI concerns

catalysts.event: Q4 FY2026 results — revenue $6.72B (+30%), non-GAAP EPS $1.82 (+37%), 27% dividend increase
Q1 FY2027 earnings and initial FY2027 outlook
300+ layer 3D NAND and GAA logic transitions at leading fabs

key_risks: WFE spending is highly cyclical; current upcycle may peak in FY2026–2027
China export controls: ~30% of revenue historically exposed to China restrictions
Customer concentration: TSMC, Samsung, and SK hynix represent the bulk of orders
Competition from Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, and KLA in adjacent process steps
Stock has run from 52-week lows; valuation leaves limited margin of safety at ~48x P/E
